2025-06-24.content:
Big things done today!
So, there's a company who normally gets all of their data through TCN, but now they want to get some additional metadata fields which they provide through an excel upload on SFTP nightly. So what I had to do was download the excel files daily uploaded on S3, then store the values into a mongodb collection. There are a lot of redundant files, so I had to scan for duplicates. Once this is filled, I match the values of this collection with the ingested db data. There's a common TCN_ID which I had to locate for both collection as they had diff names. I map the additional metadata fields to the ingested collection and append to both the dialer and call Metadata. The dialerMetadata is linked to the ProInsight UI, so after I make some tweaks to the frontend config to allow these fields, the new metadata fields are reflected in the UI now. I did it for all past data from June 1, and now I wrote a script to perform this action daily. Fun stuff!
From June 1 to June 24, there were around 42k entries which I mapped to past June data.
One minor bug: 
The forwarding metadata is reflected twice on the UI for some reason, need to check it out.

Boot up a redis server for storing redis dump
Run client.py to actually interact with the server and get responses

I created my own agent, and saw how as an Evaluator, you basically prompt cekura how it should talk to your voice agent, what scenarios it should test, then at the end it gives you results. 
NOW, to connect your agent to cekura, you’d need a link, that link is added on cekura, but sampat configured it to include MY link, which here is an ngrok (my old friend) that I opened on my device exposing my running server. The result? I keep an ngrok link and customllm server running, and I can create and test scenarios on Cekura with my prompts and check changes. Whew.

Iterated on the 2 FSA things which was unfinished yesterday, DNC and Name verification. Kashish sat me down and told me to have a clear testing approach whenever there’s an identified bug, which I will list below:


Obtain information about an issue in the agent
Try to replicate this issue locally, whether on text or on call. If the issue occurs on call then you have a transcript to analyse.
If the issue is not replicable, run sufficient number of call/text iterations to confirm the same.
If the issue is replicable, then identify the prompt sections causing the issues, update it and check again. Iterate this process.
To confirm the prompt changes solved the issue, run MULTIPLE text AND call iterations to confirm the same.
Ensure these local calls are logged in Cekura, so that their transcript can be viewed later
Yeah so I followed this to fix the pesky name verification issue - added the specific line in the top guardrail of the general prompt. Then went with a v simplified DNC. So that’s DONE. Oh I wrote simulations also for it yesterday.

Interesting day. I found out essentially that my main task rn is to work on enabling the 1FA agent for in hours too. Deadlines are set, so I started working, found a few issues. Office hours is defined at 9am-5pm Eastern time, but some agents like in Arizona have a different time. So I can't just pass in current_time simply into the context. Also the format is clunky, and there's no day of the week - Mon-Fri is business hours. These are non trivial non prompt changes.
Also, I made the change to the general prompt to make it take in and out business hours, but I feel it might perform better if there were 2 separate general prompts - one for in hours and one for out hours. These are interesting changes. Probably the biggest indication of my worth here at the company is if they let me work to help for *any* of these changes, or ask me to only focus on changing prompts. Hmm. Tomorrow will tell.

2025-08-13.content: Good day! So I deliberated about the best way to solve this in hours/ out hours issue with some form of code change. First order of business was to convert the current time in the context into a proper readable format and also add a day of the week variable. I was kinda surprised how readily Kashish agreed to this, he was like, yeah go ahead, raise a PR, it is a good change. So yesterday's ending thought went in a nice direction! Added the PR and it got merged into llm-orchestrator. My first code contribution! Was tiny, but I contributed, yaaay! I spent the rest of the day checking if this fixed the issue. Special scenarios seem to be handled, but some simulations where the user is confused makes the agent default to out of office hours state no matter what. Hm. More changes?

2025-08-14.content:
I deliberated one of two ideas to make the agent better - either a toolcall within llm-orch that keeps passing business hours status to the llm, or just calculate is_business_hours from the time and pass to the prompt as a boolean?
Simple won, easy. So I added a new variable in the context and raised another PR. However, some edge cases were still defaulting to out of hours. Then I found the issue. The prompts were written with an out of office agent in mind right, so small local mentions here and there of a default ooo agent prevailed over the general prompt guidelines? Solution? Add a rule to every state's guardrail, that seemed to override the local irregularities. So thats a nice temp fix! Need to test a bit more to confirm it holds

2025-08-21.content:
Mapped out the STG flow - it's interesting. Instead of just using the phone number for lookup which is not reliable enough, based on what brought the user here, different lookups are used.
Called cause of a debt letter? Lookup with file number, if thats not found check with SSN and zipcode
Called because of email? Lookup with email address
Etc, so its interesting. Also more so because there would have to be an API that performs lookup with different sets of permutations of data fields, AND the LLM I believe would have to intelligently send only those arguments which are relevant to the lookup for that moment to the API. So it's interesting stuff.

2025-08-22.content:

Then I updated my setup to the latest commit, it had been a while. Debugged some issues, then I tested the API.
And it worked! There were issues, yes, but the core logic of the LLM passing in certain arguments in certain scenarios to do the lookup worked. So that's encouraging.

2025-09-11.content:
Came in early because I had to leave early today. My work today was on the TRK agent, to make a test agent for that. There was a new state would be dynamically decided based on the presence of a variable, but because there was no data for this tenant in the DB yet, I had to use mock data in the prompt itself. This meant I could not do dynamic routing, and after discussion with the PM I decided to make 2 agents, one which has placed agency info and one which does not.
Having faced this problem before too, I talked to the Backend Engineer about the using of mock data and how much effort is needed to insert new data into the dev db.
Turns out, data with a schema other than that of the DB would require a lot of effort to sync with Postgres etc.
So I suggested an idea - why not have a mock server, somewhere where I can just upload JSON files with any schema for a tenant, and it would store it in JSON files and query from that as an API when I wanted to access it in the LLM. This would be for those new tenants whose data wasnt yet in our DB nor did we have their APIs. The benefit of this over putting data in the prompt was that while there was a latency tradeoff, you had more control here, could add multiple accounts and also query different APIs. Simply a more scalable approach. The engineer liked this approach and after conferring with the senior engineer, approved it and asked if I would work on it to implement it. I was so happy! Sounds like an interesting project for sure, which I think will help me and others for demos.

2025-09-25.content:
Planned multiple things, but majority of the day went in testing and hammering gpt 4o. What I assumed to be a straightforward prompt fix turned out be very stubborn, as gpt REFUSED to transition to the next state after the dynamic prompt state. It was either aggressively triggering call end, or staying in the same state. This was a reproducible unfixable issue no matter what prompt change. I tried changing the state change tool call description to be more robust but to no avail. Claude sonnet 3.5,3.7 and 4 worked perfectly. 4o seems just not good enough for more advanced tool calling.
Other than that, I pushed for a review of the mock server code I had written with the Backend engineer. He reviewed and modified it, basically built on it and made it prod ready, and created a repo for it.

weeklySummaries.2025-W25: The first week involved onboarding, obtaining necessary software access (AWS, Databricks, GitHub), and familiarizing oneself with internal tools (Bifrost, Heimdall, Matsya).  Progress on adding two new tags (Line of Credit and Car Loan) for Curo Financial involved developing regular expressions; the Line of Credit regex is largely complete, while the Car Loan regex requires further refinement due to limitations imposed by positive/negative matching requirements.  Challenges included initial regex failures and a dependence on clarifying client requirements.  Despite some initial idling, significant progress was made in setting up the local development environment, understanding existing tag functions, and beginning the implementation of the new tags.
weeklySummaries.2025-W26: Successfully integrated a new metadata ingestion pipeline, processing 42,000 entries since June 1st.  This involved daily downloading and deduplicating Excel files from SFTP/S3, storing data in MongoDB, matching records based on TCN_ID across different databases, and updating both dialer and call metadata, reflected in the ProInsight UI after frontend configuration adjustments. A daily automated script is now in place.  Challenges included resolving naming inconsistencies across databases and a current UI bug displaying duplicate metadata.  Additionally, progress was made on refining regex rules for data tagging, including adding a new rule for Auto Loan identification and creating rules for Customer Self Payment and High Risk Language using Claude.  Future work involves addressing the UI bug and exploring less restrictive methods for regex-based tagging.  A local tunneling setup guide was also created.
weeklySummaries.2025-W27: This week saw significant progress in integrating and testing LLM-powered voice agents.  Despite initial concerns about a purely NLP-focused role, the author successfully set up a local development environment encompassing Redis, a Uvicorn server, and a webhook connecting to Cekura for voice analysis.  A key achievement was establishing a system to test LLM responses by simulating previous conversation segments, though this currently requires cumbersome JSON editing, presenting an opportunity for future tool development.  Challenges included initial difficulties debugging the conversation simulation and navigating the Cekura interface.  The author also created and documented a comprehensive tag database and  successfully automated a weekly Excel report generation.  Finally, the author's prompt engineering document received unexpected positive attention from the CEO, necessitating further refinement.

A document for maintaining simulation names and scenarios was created, and prompts for a new client were integrated. A key achievement was successfully connecting the local system to Cekura for voice agent prompt simulation. However, progress was hampered by recurring API issues that required substantial debugging effort. Time was also lost due to feeling unwell one day. Despite these challenges, the week ended on a high note with recognition from the CEO during an all-hands meeting and a celebratory dinner.

weeklySummaries.2025-W35: This week saw progress in prompt standardization and agent functionality, alongside addressing critical production issues. Achievements include drafting an internal note on prompt standardization strategy aiming for a common base template with dynamic variables, debugging and resolving a broken production testing number by identifying and correcting a misconfigured API endpoint (earning positive feedback), and improving the STG agent prompts with enhanced fuzzy matching and intelligent user responses. Challenges included initial blockage on STG API access, delayed deployment of an agent fix, and the need to add custom parameters to the general transfer_call tool. Progress was made on adding a custom parameter to the transfer_call tool, with code changes and testing completed, and initial setup work was started for three new agents, although blocked by data availability. The team also held productive discussions on prompt standardization, focusing on unifying sections across prompts and tenants.
weeklySummaries.2025-W37: This week involved significant progress on multiple agent projects. The successful PPW demo was a major achievement, incorporating payroll deduction handling and positive customer feedback, while STG testing revealed a need for TTS adjustments. Development of the TRK agent faced challenges due to missing tenant data, leading to a workaround involving two separate agents and a proposal for a mock server to handle dynamic data with varying schemas, which was approved for implementation. Work on inbound and outbound agents included refining data accuracy, adding context, improving politeness, and setting up integration with Zaheer for call triggering, culminating in a successful demo and positive feedback.
weeklySummaries.2025-W36: Over the past week, significant progress was made on agent development and standardization efforts.  Achievements include simplifying the STG agent for Phase 1, porting and modifying the UFL agent to meet specific requirements and create a demo version, and successfully implementing a code change for custom parameters in general tools. A comprehensive document outlining a new prompt standardization architecture was also created, presented, and approved for a POC using Jinja templating. Challenges encountered involved resolving local deployment errors, addressing SSL certificate issues, and adapting to evolving STG agent requirements.  The focus moving forward is on completing the STG and TRK agent modifications, and developing the prompt standardization POC.

## Executive Summary

This individual demonstrates strong technical skills and a proactive approach to problem-solving in the realm of agent engineering. A recurring theme is the frustration experienced with GPT-4o's unreliability compared to Claude, alongside a consistent drive to automate and improve existing processes. The focus should be on streamlining workflows, mitigating GPT-4o related issues, and strategically prioritizing tasks for optimal impact.

## Key Accomplishments

*   **Mock Server API Contribution (2025-09-26):** Developed and implemented a mock inbound Webhook API call to simulate fetching user details, a significant code contribution that was promptly accepted. *Impact: Enables more realistic testing and development of agent interactions.*
*   **STG Reporting Automation (2025-09-24):** Successfully automated the generation and distribution of daily STG stats via email. *Impact: Improves transparency and awareness of agent performance, enabling faster response to issues.*
*   **STG Agent Launch (2025-09-18):** Successfully launched Phase 1 of the STG agent after a month of work. *Impact: Delivers a functional agent that is ready for deployment and scaling.*
*   **Prompt Standardization Architecture (2025-W36):** Created and presented a comprehensive document outlining a new prompt standardization architecture. *Impact: Promotes consistency and efficiency in prompt development across different agents.*
*   **Resolved Production Testing Number (2025-W35):** Debugged and resolved a broken production testing number by identifying and correcting a misconfigured API endpoint. *Impact: Ensured the continuity of testing and development processes.*

## Critical Challenges

1.  **GPT-4o Unreliability:** Repeatedly encounters issues with GPT-4o's inconsistent behavior and inability to handle complex tool calling, leading to wasted time and the need to switch to Claude. *Root Cause: GPT-4o's model architecture or training data may not be as suitable for certain conversational AI tasks compared to Claude, or could involve undiagnosed integration issues.*
2.  **Data Availability and Mock Server Dependencies:** Reliant on external data sources and the mock server for agent development, leading to delays when data is missing or the mock server needs modifications. *Root Cause: Inadequate data infrastructure and a lack of readily available data for testing and development, creating a bottleneck in the workflow.*
3.  **Iterative Feedback Loops & Shifting Priorities:** Experiences frequent feedback cycles and changes in project priorities, potentially impacting overall efficiency and focus. *Root Cause: Fluid project requirements and evolving priorities impacting workflows.*

## Behavioral Patterns

*   **Proactive Problem Solver:** Actively seeks solutions to challenges, such as developing workarounds for data limitations and automating reporting processes.
*   **Code Contributor:** Confidently contributes code to projects, as demonstrated by the mock server API and STG reporting automation.
*   **Documentation and Standardization Advocate:** Creates documentation and proposes standardization initiatives, showing a commitment to knowledge sharing and efficiency.
*   **Frustration with GPT-4o:** Expresses frustration with GPT-4o's performance issues, indicating a need for more reliable tools or strategies for mitigating its limitations.
*   **Driven to Automate:** Proactively seeks opportunities to automate repetitive tasks, such as reporting and data processing.

## Strategic Recommendations

1.  **Develop a GPT-4o Mitigation Strategy:** Document specific GPT-4o failure modes and implement a checklist of tests to run *before* committing to GPT-4o in a new agent. Include a fallback mechanism to Claude when GPT-4o proves unreliable.
2.  **Prioritize Mock Server Enhancements:** Advocate for a dedicated resource to maintain and enhance the mock server, including features like data generation and version control.
3.  **Establish Clear Project Prioritization Criteria:** Work with stakeholders to define clear criteria for prioritizing projects and tasks. Implement a system for managing changes in priority to minimize disruptions.
4.  **Streamline Data Access:** Collaborate with data engineers to improve data availability for agent development and testing. Explore options for creating synthetic data sets to reduce reliance on external sources.
5.  **Optimize Feedback Loops:** Establish clear expectations for feedback cycles and ensure that feedback is specific, actionable, and timely. Consider incorporating automated testing and validation to reduce the need for manual feedback.
6.  **Time Blocking:** Implement time-blocking strategies to focus on high-priority tasks and minimize distractions. Allocate specific blocks of time for coding, testing, and meetings.
7.  **Communicate Technical Limitations:** Proactively communicate the limitations of GPT-4o and other tools to stakeholders, managing expectations and influencing project decisions.

## Growth Opportunities

1.  **Agent Orchestration & Architecture:** Deepen understanding of agent orchestration principles and architecture to design more robust and scalable solutions.
2.  **Prompt Engineering Expertise:** Expand knowledge of advanced prompt engineering techniques, including few-shot learning, chain-of-thought prompting, and prompt optimization for different LLMs.

## 30-Day Focus Plan

1.  **GPT-4o Mitigation Strategy (Week 1):** Document GPT-4o failure modes and create a fallback mechanism to Claude.
2.  **Mock Server Enhancement Proposal (Week 2):** Develop a proposal for mock server enhancements, including data generation and version control.
3.  **Data Access Improvement Plan (Week 3):** Collaborate with data engineers to improve data availability for agent development and testing.
4.  **Project Prioritization Criteria (Week 4):** Work with stakeholders to define clear criteria for prioritizing projects and tasks.
